title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen (GQA/MQA tuning, kernels, KV cache, continuous batching)
author: Ayesha Khan
description:
Motivation: Several customer workloads and internal benchmarks showed suboptimal tail latency and token throughput for specific open models (Llama 2 variants, Mistral-7B, and Qwen series). Root causes include: (1) incorrect kernel selection for Multi-Query Attention (MQA) vs Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) variants, (2) KV cache layout penalties when switching between per-layer and fused cache formats, (3) continuous batching heuristics that do not respect model-specific sequence-length and quantization profiles, and (4) quantized operator paths that regress on Qwen-like attention shapes.

Summary of changes: single PR that groups a set of runtime, scheduler and kernel improvements scoped to model-specific quirks. The high level items are: 
- Kernel selection: introduce model-aware kernel picker that prefers fused attention kernels for Llama/Mistral when sequence length > 512 and switches to low-latency MQA kernels for Qwen variants. This reduces unnecessary kernel warm-ups and avoids fallback slow paths.
- KV cache packing: add a lightweight conversion path to transform per-layer KV layout to the runtime-fused format on first request for models with large number of heads (Qwen). The conversion is cached per model-version to avoid amortized pain.
- Continuous batching: scheduler improvements to group requests by target model variant, quantization profile (GQA vs MQA), and sequence length bucket. This preserves latency SLOs for short requests while increasing batching efficiency for long requests.
- Quantization operator tuning: adjust 4-bit/8-bit matmul microkernel tiling parameters when running Qwen-shaped attention to avoid denormalization stalls on certain GPUs; small change but measurable in p50/p95.
- Heuristics and flags: add per-model metadata flags (mqatype: MQA|GQA|AUTO) and a runtime fallback to AUTO detection based on model config and first inference trace.

Benchmarks: end-to-end benchmarks run on our perf-canary infra (A100 and H100 nodes) show: median token latency down 9-18% for Llama-family and Mistral when sequences > 512, p95 down 12% for Qwen workloads, and throughput up 5-22% depending on batch composition. The conversion-path adds ~0.5-1ms on the first request for converted models but is cached thereafter.

Compatibility and safety: changes are backward-compatible by default. All new heuristics are behind config flags. There is an opt-out cluster-wide feature flag (runtime.model-quirk-tuning=false) and per-deployment control in Dedicated/Private.

Testing: unit tests for kernel picker, KV cache converter, and scheduler bucketing added. End-to-end smoke tests against redwood-examples/chat and perf-canary scripts added. Repro infra tests that found regression are now covered.

Files changed overview: small to-medium changes across runtime kernel selection, scheduler, kv-cache module, and model metadata. No user-facing API changes.

Related: Linear tickets ENG-1345 (GQA/MQA routing), ENG-2910 (kv cache layout conversion), PM-402 (perf cadence for model-specific tuning).

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to cache invalidation semantics in kv_cache/convert.py and interaction with rolling upgrades. The scheduler changes are additive but touch hot paths; profiling results included in the benchmark artifacts.

release_notes: Model-specific runtime optimizations: improved latency and throughput for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen variants. Adds model-aware kernel picker, on-demand KV cache layout conversion, continuous-batcher grouping by model/quant-profile/seq-length, and quant-operator tiling tweaks. Backwards compatible and behind runtime flags.
